headline: Approved stock transfer and manager change at Cape Ann Convenience, 1 Main St.; approved Boulevard Variety license transfer at 33 Western Ave.; approved special event liquor permits.
summary: The board approved license transfers, ownership and manager changes, outdoor entertainment extensions, a farmers market permit, and special event alcohol permits. It continued the Gloucester Restaurant Group (Mehfil) license petition and the Zorba Kinigstein change of hours petition. A motion to approve the Sugar Mags Inc. beer and wine license failed 0-2.
decisions: Approved the change of ownership interest and change of manager at 3019, LLC, dba Cape Ann Convenience, 1 Main St., 2-0.
Approved the transfer of license from Dogtown Variety Inc., dba Boulevard Variety, to SCD Enterprises Inc., dba Boulevard Variety, at 33 Western Ave., 2-0.
Continued the petition of Gloucester Restaurant Group, dba Mehfil, for a proposed new Annual Section 12 All Alcoholic Beverages License at 50 Rogers St., 2-0.
Motion to approve the proposed new Annual Section 12 Beer and Wine License for Sugar Mags Inc. at 64 Rogers St. failed, 0-2.
Approved the one-day request by Amy Murphy to serve wine and malt beverages at a fundraiser concert at 7 Crafts Rd. on 9/19/2026 (rain date 9/20/2026), 2-0.
Approved the request by Christopher Tkach to serve wine and malt beverages during Magtoberfest on 10/11/2026 at 1 Lexington Ave., 2-0.
Approved the request by Maritime Gloucester to serve all alcoholic beverages during Schoonerfest on 9/4/2026 at 23 Harbor Lp., 2-0.
Approved the change of manager and change of officers for Gloucester Lodge 892 Bpo of Elks, 107 Atlantic Ave., with Jeffrey Martin as manager of record, 2-0.
Approved the request by Jeffrey Martin to extend entertainment to include outside at Gloucester Lodge 892 Bpo of Elks, 107 Atlantic Rd., 2-0.
Approved the request by Maria Seniti-Figurido to extend outdoor entertainment from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM at The Burn, 289 Main St., 2-0.

Approved the Farmer’s Market Permit for J & N Ventures LLC, dba Cape Ann Lanes, at Burnhams Field, 9 Sargent St., subject to submitting the MDAR form from the Department of Agricultural Resources, 2-0.
Continued the petition of Zorba Kinigstein for a change of hours for J & Z Gloucester Foods LLC, dba George’s Restaurant and Bar, 178 Washington St., 2-0.
Approved the minutes of the 6/16/2026 meeting, 2-0.

CITY OF GLOUCESTER 
                                               LICENSING BOARD MEETING 
 
HARBOR MASTERS OFFICE 
19 HARBOR LOOP #2 
GLOUCESTER MA 01930 
 
Meeting Minutes  
July 17, 2026 
 
 
Board Members Present: 
 
Melissa J. Teixeira Prince, Chairperson  
John Lamirande  
 
Also in Attendance: 
Natasha Dale, Licensing Board Clerk  
Rob Vicari, Building Commissioner  
 
Absent: 
Ted Costa 
 
 
The Chair Calls to Order the Quorum of the Licensing Board at 6:30 PM. 
 
The Chair reads the following statement; 
 Effective August 16, 2023 the public is welcome to attend our meetings in person. 
Alternatively, the public may attend through the zoom link listed on the agenda. The 
meeting notice will reflect if this a meeting of zoom only. As the recent amendments to 
the Open Meeting Law allows the Committee can continue to hold the meeting remotely. 
Please note that the in person meeting will not be suspended or terminated if 
technological problems interrupt the remote connection.  
 
Public Hearing: 
 
Change of Ownership Interest and a Change of Manager at 3019, LLC, dba Cape Ann 
Convenience, 1 Main St. Manager of Record: Meghnaben P. Patel 
 
Jackson Christian, Attorney for 3019, LLC 
 
Mr. Christian states that this application is for a stock transfer. Bhikhabai Patel is 
transferring 20% of his interest in the LLC to Meghnaben Patel. The other shareholder 
Alpa Patel is going to be transferring his interest entirely to Meghnaben.
Alpa was the approved manager of record for the license and will be transferring the 
manager of record to Meghnaben and approve Bhikhabai to be the manager of the LLC.  
 
Meghnaben will be a 45% owner of the LLC with Bhikhabai owning the other 55%.  
 
This will be Meghnaben’s first license within the City of Gloucester.  
 
There will be a minimum of two people working at a time. There is a camera by the 
counter where you can see every aisle in the store. The store is between 16 and 1800 
square feet.  
 
Ms. Patel is planning to be at the store about 40 hours a week. When Ms. Patel is not 
there other employees will be in charge. If something happens when Ms. Patel is not in 
the store her employees can call her cell phone.  
 
The sale of alcohol on the premise will be Monday- Saturday 8:00 AM- 11:00 PM and 
Sunday from 10:00 AM-11:00 PM. 
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the change of Ownership Interest and a Change of Manager 
at 3019, LLC, dba Cape Ann Convenience, 1 Main St. Manager of Record: Meghnaben 
P. Patel 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
 
Continued Business: 
 
Petition of SCD Enterprises on a Transfer of License from Dogtown Variety Inc., dba 
Boulevard Variety to SCD Enterprises Inc., dba Boulevard Variety at 33 Western Ave. 
Manager of Record: Joseph Youssef 
 
Attorney Tom Truaxx, Salem and Joseph Youseff, Gloucester are present 
 
Mr. Youssef is going to now be the sole owner, officer, shareholder and director for the 
new corporation.  
 
Currently Ms. Youssef has 50% ownership with Albert Abdelmalak. Mr. Abdelmalak has 
came across some financial issues and is selling off his corporations, including 
Boulevard Variety.  
 
Mr. Youssef has purchased an updated card reader and has caught a handful of fake id’s 
since purchasing.
The old owner has left Mr. Youssef with an outstanding bank loan, unpaid alcohol 
distributor bills and $45,000 is electric bills. Mr. Youssef had made an agreement with 
the electric company to pay that down monthly once the transaction is approved. Mr. 
Youssef has also already paid off the owed money for the alcohol distributors.  
 
There are cameras near the register and outside. There is no signage in the store stating 
that there are cameras recording them. 
 
The public only has one entrance and one exit.  
 
The chair opens public hearing. 
Speaking in favor: none 
Speaking in opposition: none 
The chair closes public hearing.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of SCD Enterprises on a Transfer of License 
from Dogtown Variety Inc., dba Boulevard Variety to SCD Enterprises Inc., dba 
Boulevard Variety at 33 Western Ave. Manager of Record: Joseph Youssef 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Petition of Gloucester Restaurant Group, dba Mehfil on a proposed new Annual, Section 
12 All Alcoholic Beverages License at 50 Rogers St. Manager of Record: Prabjhot 
Pabla 
 
Jackson Christian, Lynn 
Jaspreet Pabla, 63 Lepore St., Methuen 
Jacob Simmons, 50 Rogers St., representing the property owners 
 
Prabjhot Pabla has gained experience in alcohol sales as the assistant manager at 
Ragini, Mr. and Mrs. Pablas other restaurant.  
 
Ms. Prince states that when we left off before there were several concerns about the 
property, both upstairs and downstairs.  
 
A walk through was conducted with Rob, Natasha, Board of Health, the contractor and 
both Mr. and Mrs. Pabla. Mr. Christian states that there are 4 big issues that were 
discussed at the walk through. Bringing the property up to ADA compliance, 
sprinklering the building, condition of the windows and the HVAC. 
 
 
The estimate the contractor provided the board states that the total cost of the work 
needed to be done will be around $82,000. All of the coolers in the restaurant are 
working properly. Mr. Pabla states that the air conditioning is working.
Mr. Vicari suggests doing the food plan with the Board of Health to get a better estimate 
of how much work the space needs. He also mentions based on the number of 
bathrooms the occupancy will only be 75 people, not 90 including staff.  
 
Mr. Pabla and his team is predicting about a 12-14 week turnaround to open the 
restaurant.  
 
Ms. Prince states that the applicant needs to resubmit a new adjusted application with 
the correct occupancy number and kitchen/ bathroom plans.  
 
There will not be any structural changes happening inside besides adding a host area 
right in the entrance.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to continue the petition of Gloucester Restaurant Group, dba Mehfil on 
a proposed new Annual, Section 12 All Alcoholic Beverages License at 50 Rogers St. 
Manager of Record: Prabjhot Pabla 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Petition of Sugar Mags Inc., on a proposed new Annual, Section 12 Beer and Wine 
License at 64 Rogers St. Manager of Record: Melissa Sallah 
 
Ms. Prince states that this application will not be heard as there is already a current 
liquor license at this location. 
 
Ms. Prince moves to approve the petition of Sugar Mags Inc., on a proposed new 
Annual, Section 12 Beer and Wine License at 64 Rogers St. Manager of Record: Melissa 
Sallah 
 
Mr. Costa seconds 
All in favor, 0-2 
 
Special One Day Liquor License:  
 
Petition of Amy Murphy requesting to serve wine and malt beverages only during a 
Fundraiser Concert event to benefit Action on 9/19/2026 with a rain date on 9/20/2026 
from 4:00 PM- 9:00 PM at 7 Crafts Rd. 
 
Amy Murphy, 14 Hutchins Ct., Gloucester is present on zoom. 
 
Ms. Murphy is requesting a one day liquor license for the 2nd annual benefit concert for 
Action Inc. Ms. Murphy states that last years event was a huge success and they raised 
over $8,000. This year it will be the same format except they are planning to use True 
North Brewing instead of Rockport Brewing. True North will be serving beer, wine and 
complimentary non-alcoholic beverages as well. All proceeds will go to Action Inc.
Ms. Murphy is anticipating about 170 people to attend.  
 
Guests will use the parking lot out front of Grand Banks and Nichols Candy has also 
given them permission to use their lot as well.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of Amy Murphy requesting to serve wine and 
malt beverages only during a Fundraiser Concert event to benefit Action on 9/19/2026 
with a rain date on 9/20/2026 from 4:00 PM- 9:00 PM at 7 Crafts Rd. 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Petition of Christopher Tkach requesting to serve wine and malt beverages only during 
Magtoberfest on 10/11/2026 from 11:00 AM- 5:00 PM at 1 Lexington Ave.  
 
Christopher Tkach, 89 Commercial St., Malden 
Kiley Davis, 22 Magnolia Ave., Gloucester 
 
Ms. Davis states that Idle Hands Brewing will be taking over the annual Magtoberfest 
celebrations as in years past it has been Notch Brewing.  
 
There will be no truck, but instead there will be a table and a tent in an entirely closed 
area beer garden. There will be signs at the entrance to the beer garden and security 
checking id’s at the entrance. 
 
There is no rain date for the event. 
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of Christopher Tkach requesting to serve wine 
and malt beverages only during Magtoberfest on 10/11/2026 from 11:00 AM- 5:00 PM 
at 1 Lexington Ave.  
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Petition of Maritime Gloucester requesting to serve All Alcoholic Beverages during 
Schoonerfest on 9/4/2026 from 5:00 PM- 10:00 PM at 23 Harbor Lp. 
 
Isabel Pett, 12 Beach Rd., Gloucester is present. 
 
Ms. Pett states that this event happens every year and there are no changes. There will 
be about 4 TIPS certified bartenders.  
 
Ms. Pett is requesting a full liquor license. Everyone is volunteers. The event is invite 
only with no rain date.
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of Maritime Gloucester requesting to serve All 
Alcoholic Beverages during Schoonerfest on 9/4/2026 from 5:00 PM- 10:00 PM at 23 
Harbor Lp. 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Change of Manager: 
 
Petition of Gloucester Lodge 892 Bpo of Elks, 107 Atlantic Ave. on a change of 
Manager and Change of Officers. Manager of Record: Jeffrey Martin 
 
Jeffrey Martin, 24 Haskell St., Gloucester is present on zoom. 
 
Mr. Martin has never been a bar manager, but has bartended before.  
 
For the past 5 years Mr. Martin has been a trustee of the lodge. When the bar manager 
left Mr. Martin stepped up to take on the role.  
 
Mr. Martin is working on receiving his TIPS and Crowd Control certificates.  
 
Mr. Martin is planning to spend about 40 hours a week at the lodge. All employees have 
Mr. Martin’s phone number if he is needed when he is not at the lodge. Mr. Martin does 
have one daytime bartender that has experience receiving deliveries.  
 
The premises is only licensed for indoors. 
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of Gloucester Lodge 892 Bpo of Elks, 107 
Atlantic Ave. on a change of Manager and Change of Officers. Manager of Record: 
Jeffrey Martin 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Extension of Entertainment: 
 
Application of Jeffrey Martin requesting to extend his entertainment to include outside 
at Gloucester Lodge 892 Bpo of Elks, 107 Atlantic Rd.  
 
The board previously heard this plan at our last meeting and it was approved contingent 
on Mr. Martin submitting a Change of Manager application.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the application of Jeffrey Martin requesting to extend his 
entertainment to include outside at Gloucester Lodge 892 Bpo of Elks, 107 Atlantic 
Rd.  
 
Ms. Prince seconds
All in favor, 2-0 
 
 
Application of Maria Seniti-Figurido requesting to extend outdoor entertainment from 
9:00 PM to 11:00 PM at The Burn, 289 Main St. 
 
 
Joel Favazza, Seaside Legal Solutions, 123 Main St., Gloucester is present.  
 
Mr. Favazza is present asking for approval to extend their outdoor entertainment to 
11:00 PM. All music would be acoustic or one to two person bands.  
 
There have been no prior complaints about outdoor music since the restaurant has 
opened.  
 
The outdoor music will only be seasonally. The patio is closed during the winter months.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the application of Maria Seniti-Figurido requesting to 
extend outdoor entertainment from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM at The Burn, 289 Main St. 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Farmer’s Market Permit Approval: 
 
Petition of J & N Ventures LLC, dba Cape Ann Lanes on a proposed Farmer’s Market 
Permit on Wednesdays during the Backyard Growcery until September 30, 2026 at 
Burnhams Field, 9 Sargent St.  
 
Nic Pzenny, 30 Dodge St., Gloucester is present on zoom.  
 
Mr. Pzenny is requesting to sell 4 packs of canned beer and seltzer at the Backyard 
Growcery at Burnham’s field on Wednesdays into September.  
 
Cape Ann Lanes is licensed as a pub brewer and they have a transportation permit.  
 
Legislation was recently passed to allow pub brewers to sell at farmers markets.  
 
Mr. Pzenny did not submit a MDAR form from the Department of Agricultural 
Resources.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of J & N Ventures LLC, dba Cape Ann Lanes on 
a proposed Farmer’s Market Permit on Wednesdays during the Backyard Growcery until 
September 30, 2026 at Burnhams Field, 9 Sargent St. subject to submitting the 
MDAR form from the Department of Agricultural Resources.  
 
Ms. Prince seconds
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Change of Hours: 
 
Petition of Zorba Kinigstein on a change of hours for J & Z Gloucester Foods LLC, dba 
George’s Restaurant and Bar, 178 Washington St. 
 
Zorba Kingstein, 594 Western Ave., Gloucester is present on zoom.  
 
Mr. Kinigstein has attempted over the last couple of months to find some new cooks, but 
has not had any luck. Mr. Knigstein does not have the staff to do dinners right now and 
wants to get into compliance with the hours that they are currently open. 
 
Mr. Kinigstein will be opening for alcohol service at 8:00 AM Monday- Saturday and 
10:00 AM on Sundays and will be closing at 3:00 PM Monday- Saturday and 4:00 PM 
on Sundays.  
 
Mr. Kinigstein states that the alcohol sales have been lower since stopping dinner 
service. He pulled sales for the last 4 weeks and last year made $18,764 and this year 
during the same 4 weeks he made $10,338. He went down from 8,872 guests to 7,238 
guests.  
 
Ms. Prince states that she would like for Mr. Kinigstein to attempt to eventually be open 
for dinner service.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to continue the Petition of Zorba Kinigstein on a change of hours for J 
& Z Gloucester Foods LLC, dba George’s Restaurant and Bar, 178 Washington St. 
 
Ms. Prince seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Approval of Minutes: 
 
Ms. Prince moves to approve the minutes from the 6/16/2026 meeting. 
Mr. Costa seconds 
All in favor, 2-0 
 
Adjournment:  
 
Ms. Prince moves to adjourn at 9:33 PM 
Mr. Costa seconds 
All in favor, 2-0
